title: The Declassified '28 Pages' on Saudi Links
summary: Part IV of the 2002 Joint Inquiry into pre-9/11 intelligence, redacted at the Bush administration's insistence and released after a 13-year bipartisan push. Summarizes investigative LEADS about Saudi officials' and suspected agents' financial/logistical support to hijackers — and reaches no conclusions. The White House, Kean/Hamilton and the 2015 9/11 Review Commission all said the pages contain no evidence of institutional Saudi government funding of al-Qaeda.
tldr: The declassified 28 pages show the 2002 Joint Inquiry found FBI/CIA documents suggesting specific foreign support for some 9/11 hijackers while in the US — but it made no final determination on reliability and referred the matter to the agencies.
ai_summary:
AI review of Part Four of the Joint Inquiry report (H. Rept. 107-792, via govinfo), read in full:
- Finding 20: the Inquiry 'developed information suggesting specific sources of foreign support for some of the September 11 hijackers while they were in the United States.'
- Neither CIA nor FBI officials could address the extent of such support definitively — whether knowing or inadvertent.
- The Inquiry did NOT independently assess the accuracy of the material ('beyond the scope'); it referred a detailed compilation to the FBI and CIA for further investigation.
- Explicitly 'made no final determinations as to the reliability or sufficiency' of the information; further investigation could reveal 'legitimate, and innocent, explanations.'
- Called the intelligence gap 'unacceptable, given the magnitude and immediacy of the potential risk.' Record summary verified accurate.
